mode.title: How do you want to use {{app}}?
mode.subtitle: Answer once. You can change later, and what is in this browser stays in it.
mode.browserBody: The database sits in here, with no account and no password. It works with no internet and nothing leaves this device.
mode.browserCaveat: There is no copy: clear the site data or move to another device and there is no getting it back.
mode.browserLater: You can turn the automatic backup on later, without losing what is already here.
mode.demoHint: Made up accounts and records, to see the application full before writing anything of yours. You can erase it later.
mode.syncBody: The same data on the phone and on the computer. You choose where it lives, and it is not here: {{app}} holds nobody's data.
mode.serverWayBody: You bring {{app}} up with Docker, on your own machine or on a rented one, and sign in with email and password from any device. It is also what lets you split bills with other people.
mode.databaseWayBody: No server at all. You create a database of your own on a service like Turso, paste the address and the token on the next screen, and this browser keeps a copy there. It is there for the day this browser loses the data, and you are the one who brings it back: download a copy under Data now and then, and keep the file. A new device does not read what is in the database on its own.
mode.serverAddressHint: The same address that shows up when you bring {{app}} up with Docker.
mode.changeLater: Your choice is kept in this browser. To change it later, go to Data.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.signUpAction: Create the account and sign in
signIn.toSignUp: I do not have an account yet
signIn.signInFailed: The email or the password does not match.
signIn.signUpFailed: I could not create the account. That email may already be taken.
signIn.unreachable: I could not reach {{server}}. Check that the server is up and that the address is right.
signIn.useThisDevice: I would rather keep it on this device
signIn.firstNobodyTitle: This server has nobody on it yet
signIn.firstNobodyBody: The password is the one you choose now. It comes from nowhere and is written nowhere: it lives encrypted in the database of your server, and only you know it.
signIn.proof: Before the password is checked, this browser solves a small puzzle that takes a moment. It goes nowhere: it is there so that a robot trying thousands of passwords pays that moment on every attempt.

invitation.title: Invitation
invitation.headline: {{name}} invited you to the {{space}} space
invitation.needsServerBody: Invitations live on the server of whoever sent them. Connect this browser to a server and open the link again.
invitation.cannotOpenTitle: I could not open the invitation

projection.nothingHeadline: There is not enough to project yet
projection.detail: In {{month}}, {{income}} comes in and {{expense}} goes out, from what is already written, what repeats and your usual month.
projection.nothingDetail: Write a few months down and the projection appears by itself.
projection.yoursOnly: Your own records only. The months ahead are made of what you yourself wrote.
projection.chartDescription: The balance over the next {{count}} months.
projection.chartLegend: The line is the balance at the end of each month. Where it crosses the dashes, the money has run out.
projection.chartLegendWith: The solid line is with {{name}}. The dotted one is how it stands today.
projection.scenariosBody: A scenario is a question: what if I spend ten per cent less, what if I earn 300 more from March. It changes nothing that is written down, only the arithmetic on this screen.
projection.scenarioDescription: One change per scenario, applied to every month from the one you choose.
projection.changePercentHint: 10 adds a tenth. A negative number takes the same share off.
projection.changeAmountHint: Added every month. Negative to take away.
projection.madeOf: Every month is made of three things: what is already certain for it, which is the bills written down and the card invoices falling due in it, what repeats every month, and your usual month for the rest. The last one is the only one that can be wrong.
projection.caption: The projection month by month, with income, expense, difference and balance
projection.emptyBody: The projection uses what you have already written down. Record a few months and it appears.
projection.thinHistoryBody: I have only {{count}} months to work your usual month out from, so the habit is an educated guess. The more months you record, the better it gets.
projection.partOfMonth: In the month you are in, the habit counts only the days still to come, because today's balance already holds the days that have gone.

investments.headline: You have {{amount}} put aside
investments.detail: You put in {{invested}} and you are {{percent}} per cent above that.
investments.nothingDetail: Write down what you already have and follow whether it is earning anything.
investments.addDescription: The price is typed by you. Nothing is looked up at any broker.
investments.name: Name
investments.accountHint: Usually an investment account, but it can be any of them.
investments.quantityHint: How many units or shares. A comma or a period for the decimals, and there may be more than two.
investments.costHint: Left empty, I take it to have cost what it is worth today.
investments.newPriceDescription: The old price is kept, so the holding has a line and not only a number.
investments.caption: Holdings, with quantity, price, value and gain
investments.againstBody: The same money, earning what the CDI actually earned, month by month. The numbers come from the Banco Central and are only fetched when you ask.
investments.noIndicesTitle: I do not have the indices yet
investments.noIndicesBody: Press update to fetch the CDI, the Selic and the IPCA from the Banco Central. It is a public table: nothing of yours is sent.
investments.chartDescription: Two lines: what you have, and what the same money would have earned at the CDI.
investments.chartLegend: At the CDI it would be {{cdi}}. Yours is at {{yours}}.
investments.simulatorBody: What the money you put aside turns into, if you keep putting some aside every month and it earns. Nothing here is saved.
investments.aYearHint: As a percentage. The CDI has been near 10.
investments.simulatorChart: Two lines over the years: the total and what was put in.
investments.simulatorResult: In {{years}} years you would have {{total}}, of which {{earned}} came from the growth.
investments.covers_one: What you have today covers 1 month of your current cost of living.
investments.covers_other: What you have today covers {{count}} months of your current cost of living.
investments.independence: To live on what it earns, without touching the principal, you would need {{target}}. You are {{percent}} per cent of the way there.
investments.independenceWhen: Putting aside what is set above, you would get there in {{years}} years and {{months}} months.
investments.independenceNever: Putting aside what is set above, you never get there. Raise what you put aside each month, or what it earns.
investments.emptyBody: Write down what you already have, with today's price. After that it is a price to update now and then.

reports.yoursOnly: Your own records only. This month is made of what you yourself wrote, and not of the money of the household.
reports.nothingDetail: Pick another month, or write the first record.
reports.emptyBody: With no records there is nothing to add up. Write a few and come back.
reports.flowDescription: Diagram of the path the money took: {{income}} came in and {{expense}} went out, spread across the categories.
reports.categoryCaption: Spending by category in {{month}}, with amount and share
reports.biggest: {{name}} took {{amount}}, {{share}} per cent of everything that went out.
reports.priorityDetail: {{share}} per cent of what went out was desirable or superfluous.
reports.daysDescription: Map of the days of {{month}}, each one darker the more was spent.
reports.monthsDescription: Columns of money in and money out per month, side by side.
reports.monthsCaption: Money in, money out and the difference, month by month
reports.ofWhichBenefits: Includes {{amount}} of benefits, which land on the card and are not records.

shell.opening: Opening your database on this device.
shell.failedTitle: I could not open the database
shell.failedBody: This usually means the browser is blocking storage. Try leaving the private window, or allowing site data.
shell.notPersistentTitle: The data is only in memory
shell.notPersistentBody: This browser would not let anything be written to disk, so everything goes away when the tab closes. Fine for a look around, not for real use.
shell.busyTitle: {{app}} is already open in another tab
shell.busyBody: In this mode the database is held by one tab at a time, so that no write is lost. Use the tab that is already open, or close it and try again here.
shell.chooseAgain: Choose again where the data lives

palette.title: What do you want to do?
palette.description: Find a screen, switch space, or run an action.

dashboard.headline: You have this much in {{space}}
dashboard.yoursOnly: Your own records only. You are a Logger in this space, so these figures are what you yourself put through the accounts, and not the money of the household.
dashboard.yoursOnlySomewhere: On {{day}}. One of the spaces added together here shows your own records only, so part of these figures is what you yourself wrote, and not the money of the household.
dashboard.nothingDue: Nothing due in the next fifteen days.
dashboard.headlineEverywhere: This is what you have, every space added together
dashboard.invoiceStillOwed: of the invoice that closed and fell due on {{day}}, still owed
dashboard.limitLeft: There is still this much to spend on the card:
dashboard.noLimitYet: No limit written down. Fill it in under Accounts to see how much there is left to spend.
dashboard.noQuota: No monthly allowance written down. Fill it in under Accounts to see what is left.
dashboard.noRule: No saving rule. A rule says how much of what comes in is set aside before anything else.
dashboard.landsIn_one: The next allowance lands on {{day}}, in {{count}} day.
dashboard.landsIn_other: The next allowance lands on {{day}}, in {{count}} days.
dashboard.landsInAndGoes_one: The next allowance lands on {{day}}, in {{count}} day. What is left now goes with it.
dashboard.landsInAndGoes_other: The next allowance lands on {{day}}, in {{count}} days. What is left now goes with it.
dashboard.confirmAllDescription: Say in one go that all of them happened.
dashboard.confirmAllKeepsTheDay: Each record stays on the day it was promised for, never on today, so it stays in the month and in the limit it belongs to.
dashboard.confirmAllIsFinal: There is no undoing this: a record confirmed by mistake is deleted on the records screen.
dashboard.confirmedLate_one: 1 record confirmed, on the day it was promised for.
dashboard.confirmedLate_other: {{count}} records confirmed, each on the day it was promised for.
dashboard.invoicesStillOwed: across {{count}} invoices that fell due and were not paid
dashboard.invoiceWithoutRate: No total: a purchase on this invoice is in another currency with no rate. This invoice is left out of what is still there to spend this month.
dashboard.limitInAnotherCurrency: The limit of this card is in another currency, so how much of it is left cannot be said without inventing a rate.
dashboard.invoiceClosedNotDue: of the invoice that closed, due on {{day}}
dashboard.cardsInCurrencies: in different currencies, which do not add up. The list of each one is further down.
dashboard.closedTogether: on a closed invoice, due on {{day}}
dashboard.closesAndDue: on the open invoice, closes {{closes}}, due {{due}}
dashboard.cardWithoutCycle: No closing day and no due day. Fill them in under Accounts.

notice.budgetTight: {{name}} is tight: {{left}} left for the rest of the month.
notice.billLate: {{description}} fell due {{days}} days ago and is still open: {{amount}}.
notice.savingsBehind: {{missing}} short of your savings rule this month.

budget.noneYet: A limit turns a number into a decision.
budget.yoursOnly: Your own records only. These limits are measured against what you yourself wrote, and not against the spending of the household.
budget.savingsExplain: The idea is simple: when money comes in, a part of it steps aside before any spending. Say how much and {{app}} keeps track.
budget.savingsDescription: How much steps aside every time money comes in.
budget.ruleAccountHint: The account the saved money sits in, so {{app}} can tell whether it went.
budget.ruleIsPercent: The rule is to save {{percent}} percent of what comes in.
budget.savingsBehind: Still short of the rule this month.
budget.goalsExplain: A goal points at the account its money sits in. What you saved is the balance of that account, so there is nothing to tick off by hand.
budget.newGoalDescription: What you want to put together, how much, and where that money sits.
budget.goalDateHint: Optional. With a date, {{app}} says how much a month.
budget.goalAccountHint: One account holds one goal at a time, otherwise the same money would count twice.
budget.goalNeeds: {{amount}} a month to arrive on time.
budget.newLimitDescription: A limit holds every month until you change it.
budget.amountHint: A comma or a period for the cents.
budget.stateTight: At this rate the month closes at {{amount}}.
budget.stateComfortable: {{amount}} left for the rest of the month.
budget.emptyBody: Pick what usually gets away from you, takeaway or going out. One limit on one category already changes the month.

sharing.title: Who owes whom
sharing.explain: Add up what was divided and take away what was already settled. Settling is not a record: it changes who is holding the bill, not what the house spent.
sharing.splitDescription: How {{description}} is divided between the people of the space.
sharing.sharesHint: Two and one means two thirds and one third.
sharing.incomeHint: Everybody pays in proportion to what they earn. Whoever has not said what they earn fills it in under Manage spaces, in the list of who is in the space.
sharing.paidByHint: Whoever put the money in, which is not always who wrote it down.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.createDescription: The account goes into the space {{space}}.
accounts.caption: Accounts of the {{space}} space, with name, kind, institution and balance
accounts.name: Name
accounts.balanceHint: How much is in this account today. A comma or a period for the cents.
accounts.closingDayHint: A purchase on that day or after goes on the next invoice.
accounts.dueDayHint: When the invoice has to be paid.
accounts.creditLimitHint: What the bank allows on this card. With it filled in, the Invoices screen says how much there is left to spend, counting the instalments still to come. It can be left empty.
accounts.invoiceSoFarHint: Optional. How much is already on this card's open invoice. It goes in as one record dated today on the card, which you can correct or remove later. Leave it empty if the card is new.
accounts.invoiceSoFarRecord: Invoice open when the card was written down
accounts.emptyBody: Start with the account your salary lands in. Cards, cash and investments can come later.
accounts.emptyForYou: This space has no account yet, and making one belongs to whoever runs the space.
accounts.benefitHint: VA and VR are one pot here, which is how the card usually comes. VT is another one, and so are culture and mobility.
accounts.cardComesWithIt: The card of this account is made with it. You can leave it empty.
accounts.debitMakesNoAccount: A debit card spends the balance of an account that already exists, so it makes no new account. Only the card is added.
accounts.editDescription: The kind and the currency do not change. Everything else is corrected here.
accounts.balanceEditHint: What was in this account before the first record. Changing it moves every balance from the start.
accounts.quotaHint: What lands on the card each month. Without it {{app}} cannot say what is left on it, because nothing is written when the money lands.
accounts.quotaLeftover: What is left at the end
accounts.deleteDescription: The account goes, and the cards that reached it go with it.
accounts.deleteHolds_one: There is 1 record in this account. It stays where it is, pointing at an account that is no longer there, and its money stops being counted anywhere.
accounts.deleteHolds_zero: There are no records in this account. Deleting it leaves nothing dangling.
accounts.deleteHolds_other: There are {{count}} records in this account. They stay where they are, pointing at an account that is no longer there, and their money stops being counted anywhere.
accounts.deleteInstead: If the account is simply not used any more, archiving takes it out of the way and keeps everything adding up.
accounts.knownToday: How much is on the card today
accounts.knownTodayHint: If you know, counting starts today. Left empty, the allowance of the period the card was written down in counts, less what was spent in that period.
accounts.archiveOwingBody: It still owes {{amount}}. Archived, it leaves the ways to pay.
accounts.archiveOwingStays: Its invoices stay on the overview, in the projection and under Invoices until they are paid.

rules.notABackup: That file is not a {{app}} backup. A backup comes from here, from the Download a copy button, and so does the copy this screen saves before it replaces one. A statement from the bank goes in through Import a statement.
rules.backupIsNewer: That backup was written by a newer version of {{app}}. Update this one before bringing the file back.
rules.backupHasNoSpace: That file is a backup, but there is no space inside it. There is nothing to bring back.
rules.emailTaken: That email is already in use here. Use another one.
rules.emailLooksWrong: That does not look like an email address.
rules.onePersonalSpace: You already have a personal space.
rules.accountIsArchived: That account is archived. Bring it back before writing to it.
rules.amountIsPositiveInteger: Write an amount greater than zero.
rules.transferNeedsDestination: Pick the account the money lands in.
rules.transferNeedsTwoAccounts: Moving between accounts needs two different accounts: the one the money leaves and the one it goes to.
rules.reconciledIsFrozen: That record was checked against the bank. Undo the check before changing it.
rules.categoryDepthIsTwo: A category goes inside another one and stops there. Pick one that stands on its own.
rules.categoryHasChildren: That category has others inside it. Move or delete those first.
rules.categoryIsNotItsOwnParent: A category cannot sit inside itself.
rules.categoriesAlreadyThere: This space already has categories, so the starting set was not written again.
rules.matchTextIsTooShort: Write at least two letters, otherwise the rule catches everything.
rules.recurrenceNeedsOneCurrency: A recurrence uses the currency of the space. Pick an account in it.
rules.budgetNeedsCategory: Pick the category the limit is on.
rules.budgetNeedsPriority: Pick the priority the limit is on.
rules.monthIsNotAMonth: Write the month as a year and a month.
rules.accountAlreadyHasGoal: That account already holds a goal. Use another account, or delete the goal that is there.
rules.percentIsTooLarge: There is no saving more than what comes in.
rules.splitNeedsPeople: There is nobody to divide this with: this space has one person in it.
rules.splitNeedsMembers: Somebody in this division does not belong to the space.
rules.splitNeedsShares: The shares add up to zero. Give at least one person a share.
rules.splitNeedsIncome: Nobody has said what they earn. Fill it in under Manage spaces, in the list of who is in the space, to divide by income.
rules.onlyExpensesAreSplit: Only an expense is divided, because only an expense is a cost.
rules.payerIsNotAMember: Whoever paid has to belong to the space.
rules.unknown: I could not finish that. Try again.
rules.notAllowedHere: Your role in this space does not allow that. Ask whoever runs the space, if you need to.
rules.invoiceBelongsToTheCard: An invoice is the whole of what the card will charge, so it is not read one person at a time.
rules.currencyIsSettledByTheFirstRecord: The currency of a space with records in it does not change: each record keeps the currency it was written in, and changing the space would leave the totals adding different currencies together. It can be corrected while the space is still empty.
rules.quantityIsANumber: I could not read that quantity. Write the number of units or shares on its own, like 0.125.
rules.shareIsAWholeNumber: Each share is a whole number, from zero up. Two parts for one person and one for the other is 2 and 1.
rules.percentIsANumber: I could not read that percentage. Write the number on its own, like 10 or 12.5.
rules.investmentNeedsAnAccount: An investment sits inside an account. Make one first, under Accounts.
rules.alreadyInside: You are already in this space.
rules.alreadyInvited: That person is already in the space.
rules.importNeedsTheSameCurrency: That account keeps another currency, and a file cannot be read into it yet. Pick an account in the currency of the space.
rules.invitationExpired: That invitation has expired. Ask whoever runs the space for a new one.
rules.invitationRevoked: That invitation was cancelled. Ask whoever runs the space for a new one.
rules.invitationUsed: That invitation has already been used. Each link works once.
rules.noSelfPromotion: Nobody changes their own role. Ask somebody else who runs the space.
rules.onlyOwnerTransfers: Only the Owner hands a space to somebody else.
rules.onlyTransfersHaveDestination: Only Move between accounts takes money into another account of yours. Money in or money out stays in one account.
rules.ownerRoleIsTransferred: The Owner role is not handed out like the others: it changes when the space is passed to somebody else.
rules.ownerStays: The Owner cannot be removed from their own space. Hand the space to somebody else first.
rules.personalSpaceIsPrivate: The personal space belongs to one person and takes nobody else. Make a shared space to divide anything.
rules.personalSpaceStays: The personal space does not go from here. It goes with Erase everything, which erases the whole account.
rules.rateIsRequired: A record in another currency needs the rate used on the day.
rules.tooManyAdjustments: A scenario with more than twenty changes in it is not a question anybody can read. Make two scenarios.
rules.transferBeforeLeaving: An Owner hands the space to somebody else before leaving it. Under Manage spaces, in the menu of whoever is staying.
rules.transfersAreNotSplit: A move between accounts is not split into instalments.
rules.installmentDaysAreTheirOwn: Each part of a purchase falls on its own day, so the day is changed one part at a time.
rules.notThere: I could not find that. It may have been erased, or it may be out of your reach.
rules.noConnection: I could not reach the server. Check that you are connected and try again.
rules.cardNeedsCreditAccount: Choose the invoice this card charges.
rules.cardHasNoCredit: This kind of card does not charge an invoice.
rules.cardNeedsDebitAccount: Choose the account the money leaves.
rules.cardHasNoDebit: This kind of card does not spend the balance of an account.
rules.creditAccountIsNotACard: The invoice has to be an account of the credit card kind.
rules.debitAccountIsACard: A credit card account is an invoice, not a balance.
rules.lastFourIsFourDigits: Write the last four digits of the card.
rules.cardDoesNotReachAccount: This card does not spend from that account.
rules.cardIsArchived: This card is archived. Bring it back before writing with it.
rules.benefitIsForVouchers: Only a voucher account says which benefit it is.
rules.noOpeningBalanceOnACard: A card is written down empty: what is on it is the invoice, or the monthly allowance.
rules.bundleHasNoSpace: This file has changes in it but not the space they belong to, so there is nothing to bring back.
rules.quotaIsForVouchers: Only a benefit card is credited with an amount every month. An ordinary account receives records.
rules.quotaIsPositive: What lands on a benefit card each month is a whole amount, more than nothing.
rules.quotaDayIsADayOfTheMonth: The day the allowance lands is a day of the month, from 1 to 31.
rules.notACardWithACycle: An invoice belongs to a credit card with a closing day and a due day. Fill both in under Accounts.
rules.cycleIsForCards: Only a credit card has a day it closes and a day it falls due.
rules.dayIsADayOfTheMonth: A closing day and a due day are days of the month, 1 to 31.
rules.limitIsForCards: Only a credit card has a limit.
rules.notOnAnInvoice: Only a record that is on an invoice can be moved to another one.
rules.benefitIsNotIncome: A benefit card only spends. What lands on it is the monthly allowance of the card, and {{app}} counts that on its own.
rules.benefitDoesNotLeave: Money on a benefit card is spent on the card and does not leave it. To put money on it, use Top up, on the card's line on the overview or under Accounts.
rules.closingDayTooFar: That day is too far from the expected closing. A bank moves a closing by a few days, for a weekend or a holiday; check the day, and the year.
rules.quotaNeedsADay: The allowance lands on a day of the month. Pick the day it lands on.
rules.knownAmountIsForCarryingVouchers: How much is on the card today is only for a benefit that carries. On one that resets, the monthly allowance already says what is on it.
rules.onlyAPurchaseIsRefunded: Only a purchase can be refunded.
rules.refundIsForVouchers: A refund that goes back on the card itself is for a benefit card.
rules.refundIsUpToThePurchase: A refund is more than nothing and at most what the purchase cost.
rules.cardIsNotAnOrigin: Money does not move out of a credit card into another account: what leaves a card is a purchase, on its invoice. To pay the invoice, use Pay the invoice.
rules.alreadyAMove: This record already moves money between accounts.
rules.planIsNotAMove: A part of a purchase or an occurrence of a series belongs to a plan and does not become a move between accounts.
rules.splitIsNotAMove: This record is divided between people. Undo the division first: money moved between your own accounts is not a household expense.
rules.moveEndIsNotAllowed: That account cannot be the other end. Money leaves a current account, savings or cash, and goes to one of them, to a benefit card or to a card's invoice.
rules.moveNeedsAMoneyAccount: Only money out of or into a current account, savings or cash, or a payment received on a card, becomes a move between accounts.
rules.notTheOtherHalf: That record is not the same money written on the other account. Nothing was changed.
rules.cardNeedsACycle: A credit card needs the day it closes and the day it falls due. Without them it has no invoice at all.

transactions.title: Records
transactions.caption: Records of the period, with day, description, account and amount
transactions.createDescription: Say what happened. The sign comes from the kind, so you always type a positive number.
transactions.installmentsHint: Each part lands on the right invoice of the card.
transactions.emptyBody: Change the month, or write the first record. It takes a few seconds.
transactions.noCategoriesYet: No categories yet. Create them in Categories.
transactions.priorityHint: Pick a category and the priority comes from it.
transactions.priorityFromCategory: The category says {{priority}}. Change it only when this one is different.
transactions.taught: Done. Every record with {{text}} in the description goes to that category.
transactions.aheadOfToday: That day has not arrived. The record is kept and starts counting in the balance by itself on that day, with nobody confirming it.
transactions.stillWaiting: This record was written as coming by an earlier version of the application. It counts in the balance once you say it happened.
transactions.landsOnInvoice: This goes on the {{month}} invoice, due {{day}}.
transactions.reachOnwards: This one and the ones after ({{count}})
transactions.dayIsPerPart: Each part of a purchase falls on its own day, so the day is changed one part at a time.
transactions.deleteDescription: This goes from the list, from the balances and from the reports.
transactions.deleteWholeGroup: All {{count}} instalments of {{description}} go, including the ones in months still to come.
transactions.deleteForever: There is no undo from here. If it was only the wrong category or the wrong amount, editing fixes it.
transactions.refundBody: The amount goes back on the card and comes off the spending in the purchase's category. It does not count as money coming in.
transactions.wasAMove: Did it go into an account of yours, like savings or the meal card? That is not spending:

rulesSection.title: Rules that sort on their own
rulesSection.explain: When a record arrives with no category, the first rule that matches decides for it. What you chose by hand is never replaced by a rule.
rulesSection.createDescription: Write a piece of what shows up in the description and say where it goes.
rulesSection.sorted_one: Sorted {{count}} record that had no category.
rulesSection.sorted_other: Sorted {{count}} records that had no category.
rulesSection.sorted_zero: Nothing to sort: everything already has a category.
rulesSection.sentence: When it has {{text}}, it goes to {{category}}
rulesSection.matchTextHint: Case and accents are ignored. A piece is enough, such as ifood or uber.
rulesSection.empty: No rules yet. Sort one record and use its menu to write the first one.
rulesSection.emptyAndNotYours: No rules yet. Making one belongs to whoever runs the space.

recurrences.title: What happens again
recurrences.explain: Rent, a subscription, a salary. {{app}} writes these as planned records on the right days, and they only touch the balance when you mark them as paid.
recurrences.createDescription: Say what repeats, how much and from when.
recurrences.startsOnHint: The day of this date is the day that repeats.

calendar.headline: {{month}}, the way it will happen
calendar.nothingPending: Nothing planned is left this month.
calendar.plannedLegend: What is in another colour has not happened yet.

categories.title: Categories of {{space}}
categories.createDescription: Categories sort the spending. The priority says how much it was needed.
categories.name: Name
categories.priorityHint: A starting point. Any record can disagree when it makes sense.
categories.parentHint: Two levels at most, so a subcategory takes none of its own.
categories.noParent: None, it stands on its own
categories.emptyBody: Start from the set that covers what most people spend on, then make it yours. Rename, delete and add as many as you like.

quick.label: Quick record
quick.hint: Write it in one line: what it was, how much, when and where. It reads today, yesterday, 15/09, 3x and the name of the account.

savedFilters.keepDescription: It is kept with the space and shows up on any device of yours. Nobody else sees it.
savedFilters.name: Name

theMonth.title: The month in three numbers
theMonth.headline: {{month}} in three numbers
theMonth.subtitle: For whoever is not going to log one line at a time. Say what came in, what went out and what the card asked for, and the rest of the application works exactly as it does.
theMonth.incomeHint: Wages, and everything else that landed in the account this month.
theMonth.spendingHint: Everything that went out, apart from the cards, which have the fields below.
theMonth.spendingOnlyHint: Everything that went out this month.
theMonth.whereHint: What came in and what went out both go into this one.
theMonth.clearHint: Leave a field empty to take that record away.
theMonth.nothingTyped: Write at least one of the numbers.
theMonth.savedBody: It is all in the usual places: the list, the overview, the reports and the projection. Come back here whenever you want to correct it.
theMonth.alsoTitle: This month you also logged some lines by hand
theMonth.alsoBody_one: There is 1 record written by hand in here. The numbers below go in on top of it, so do not count the same money twice.
theMonth.alsoBody_other: There are {{count}} records written by hand in here. The numbers below go in on top of them, so do not count the same money twice.
theMonth.alsoTotals: Already logged: {{income}} coming in and {{expense}} going out.
theMonth.written: What is written for this month
theMonth.caption: The records this screen wrote for {{month}}, with description, day and amount
theMonth.seeTheList: See it in the list, next to everything else
theMonth.whatItWritesHint: Nothing is kept anywhere else, or in any other shape.
theMonth.whatItWritesBody: Ordinary records: one for what came in and one for what went out, on the last day of the month, and the card one on the last day the invoice of that month still takes, which is the closing day minus one. With a card there is a fourth: paying that invoice, which leaves your account and clears the card on the day it falls due. Without it the account your wages arrive in would climb by the whole invoice every month and the card would sink by the same amount, with the total right and both accounts wrong. If the due date has not come yet, that payment goes in as planned. They all show up in the list, they count towards the balance, the budget, the reports and the projection, and you open and correct any of them exactly as you would any other record. Writing the same month again corrects these rather than writing more.
theMonth.loggerBody: This screen writes the month of the whole household, and a Logger only ever sees the records they wrote themselves. It would look empty to you even with the month already written by somebody else, and saving would count the month twice. Write your own spending through the List.
theMonth.cannotWriteBody: A Viewer sees everything and writes nothing. Ask whoever runs the space to change your role, if you need to write here.
theMonth.noAccountBody: The numbers need an account to go into. Create one and come back here.
theMonth.noAccountForYou: This space has no account yet, and making one belongs to whoever runs the space. Ask them, and come back here.
theMonth.usualBody: The middle of the {{count}} closed months before {{month}}.
theMonth.usualFigures: {{usual}} in a usual month, {{now}} in this one
theMonth.usualSame: About the same as a usual month.
theMonth.usualTooEarly: Too early in {{month}} to say. A month spends what it spends by the end of it, so this waits until the month is nearly through.
theMonth.usualTooFew: There is no usual month yet. It takes three closed months before a comparison means anything, and this space has {{count}}.
theMonth.tookBody: Only the records that carry a category. The three numbers carry none, so {{amount}} of this month is a total nobody itemised.
theMonth.tookNothing: Nothing in {{month}} carries a category. Three numbers say how much went out and cannot say what on, and that is the honest trade.
theMonth.tookLine: {{share}} per cent of what is itemised
theMonth.tookSeeReports: See every category, with the totals, in Reports
theMonth.limitsBody: Read as a whole month, because that is what these three numbers are.
theMonth.limitsTotalOnly: A limit on a category counts nothing here: the three numbers carry no category, so only a limit on everything can see them.
theMonth.invoicesHint_one: The total of the invoice that closes in {{month}}. Paying it is written too, on the day it falls due.
theMonth.invoicesHint_other: The total of each card's invoice that closes in {{month}}. Paying each is written too, on the day its card falls due.

invoice.noCardTitle: No credit card in this space
invoice.noCardBody: Add the card with the day it closes and the day it falls due. From then on every purchase lands on the right invoice, including the ones split into parts.
invoice.noCardForYou: No credit card in this space, and adding one belongs to whoever runs the space.
invoice.yoursOnlyTitle: The invoice belongs to the card
invoice.yoursOnlyBody: An invoice is the whole of what the card will charge, from everybody who used it, so it is not read one person at a time. Your own records are still under Records, the ones you put on the card among them.
invoice.noCycleBody: Without the closing day and the due day there is no way to say which invoice a purchase belongs to. Those two days are chosen when the card account is created, and there is no way to change those two days afterwards yet: delete this account and make it again with the right days.
invoice.closedHeadline_one: {{card}}: the {{month}} invoice is closed and falls due tomorrow
invoice.closedHeadline_other: {{card}}: the {{month}} invoice is closed and falls due in {{count}} days
invoice.pastHeadline_other: {{card}}: the {{month}} invoice fell due {{count}} days ago
invoice.caption: Purchases on the card {{card}} in the {{month}} invoice, with day, description and amount
invoice.inCreditHeadline: {{card}}: the {{month}} invoice is paid, and there is credit left

standing.inCredit: Paid, with credit on the card

invoice.noInterest: What was not paid stays open on this invoice. This application works out no interest and no revolving credit: the bank charges that, and its amount goes in as an ordinary record when it turns up.
invoice.payDescription: It leaves the account you choose and goes into the card.
invoice.payPartHint: It comes filled in with what is left. You can pay less, and the rest stays open on this invoice.
invoice.payOld_one: Mark the invoice before this one as paid
invoice.payOld_other: Mark the {{count}} invoices before this one as paid
invoice.payOldDescription_one: One invoice before this one is still open.
invoice.payOldDescription_other: {{count}} invoices before this one are still open.
invoice.payOldHint: Somebody who started using {{app}} with a card they already had has every old invoice sitting open, because the payments were never written down. This writes one payment for each, dated on the day it fell due.
invoice.reallyClosedOn: This invoice closed on another day
invoice.reallyClosedOnHint: The bank sometimes closes a day or two either side, because of a weekend or a holiday. Say the day it really closed and the purchases in between move to the right invoice, all at once.
invoice.countedIn: Added up in {{currency}}, at the rate written down with each purchase. Each purchase appears below in the currency it was made in.
invoice.noRateBody: A purchase on this invoice is in another currency with no rate for the day, so any total here would be a wrong number. The purchases are still in the list below. Open the purchase under Records and say what the rate was, and the total comes back.
invoice.scheduled: Payment scheduled for {{day}}. Until that day the money stays in the account and the invoice stays open:
invoice.openingDebt: Includes what the card already owed when it was written down, its opening balance:
invoice.carriedIn: Credit from the invoice before, paid in excess there:
invoice.carriedOut: Paid in excess on this invoice, and it pays the next one:
invoice.alreadyPaidTitle: One of the invoices already has a payment
invoice.alreadyPaidBody: The invoice of {{month}} already has a payment marked, and the payment does not change invoice. Moving purchases between it and the one of {{other}} leaves one with credit and the other owing more.
invoice.cardOfAnotherSpace: This card belongs to the space {{space}}.
invoice.headline: {{card}}: the {{month}} invoice

spaces.title: Your spaces
spaces.explain: Each space holds one slice of your money life. The personal one is yours alone. A shared space has members, roles and expense splitting.
spaces.createDescription: A shared space, for splitting bills with other people.
spaces.editDescription: The name, the colour and the currency of this space.
spaces.currencyHint: The currency the totals of this space are counted in. It can be changed while the space is empty: the first record decides it, because nothing is converted afterwards.
spaces.currencySettled: This space has records in it, so its currency is settled. Nothing is converted: every balance and every division already written is a number in this one.
spaces.name: Name of the space
spaces.colourHint: The colour shows in the top bar, so you always know where you are writing.

members.title: Who is in {{space}}
members.caption: Members of the {{space}} space, with role, state and monthly income
members.captionPersonal: Members of the {{space}} space, with role and state
members.incomeDescription: Used only to divide expenses in proportion to what each person earns. Leave it empty not to use it.
members.incomeHint: Nobody sees this number outside this list, and it shows up in no report.
members.inviteDescription: The person joins the {{space}} space once they open the link and accept.
members.linkReady: Done. Send this link to whoever you want in the space.
members.linkRules: Good for seven days, and for one person.
members.handOver: Hand the space to this person
members.handOverDescription: {{name}} becomes the Owner of {{space}}, and you become an Administrator.
members.handOverWarns: You cannot undo this on your own: once it is handed over, only the new Owner can hand it back. An Administrator does everything in the space except erase it and hand it on.
members.aloneBody: Invite whoever splits these bills with you. What each person sees comes from the role they get.
members.personalBody: This space is yours alone and takes no members. To split bills, create a shared space.
members.needsServerBody: In this mode the data sits in this browser alone, so there is nowhere for an invitation to point. With a server of yours, you make a link and the person comes in through it.

roles.youAre: Your role in this space is {{role}}

roleHint.admin: Does everything, except deleting the space or transferring it.
roleHint.editor: Writes and edits transactions, accounts, goals and budgets.
roleHint.viewer: Sees everything in the space and changes nothing of it. Their own monthly income stays theirs.
roleHint.logger: Writes and sees only their own records, of any kind. Meant for a child, or for whoever helps with the house.

designSystem.subtitle: Direction Papel e tinta. Every piece here is the piece that ships.

designSystem.specimenTitle: What is left until the end of the month

fields.amountHint: A comma or a period for the cents.

data.title: Data
data.importBody: Read a statement or an invoice in CSV, OFX, QIF, XLSX, JSON or PDF. You check everything before it is written.

skipped.unknownPerson_one: 1 row in {{table}} pointed at somebody this database does not know and was left out.
skipped.unknownPerson_other: {{count}} rows in {{table}} pointed at somebody this database does not know and were left out.

data.sheetBody: A copy of the records in a spreadsheet of yours, rewritten every time. One way only: the sheet shows, and {{app}} remains where the records live. To bring data back, save the sheet as XLSX or CSV and use the import.
data.sheetIdHint: Leave it empty and one is made. After the first time this field fills itself in.
data.tooLarge: That file is over {{megabytes}} MB, which is the limit. A statement of a year is a few kilobytes and a backup of a decade is a few megabytes, so a file that size is almost always something else.
data.changeModeHint: Changing takes you back to the first question. What is in this browser stays in it, and does not travel on its own: download a copy first if you want to take it with you.
data.saveCopyBody: One file with everything in the spaces you tick: records, accounts, cards, categories, budgets and goals. Keep it wherever you like.
data.backupCannot: You are neither Owner nor Administrator of this space, so it stays out.
data.bringBackBody: Reads a file you kept and joins it with what is already here.
data.bringBackNotYours: {{name}} is already here and belongs to somebody else, so this file does not go into it.
data.bringBackAdds: It only adds what is missing. Nothing already here is removed or replaced, and opening the same file twice duplicates nothing.
data.restoreNotYours: This file carries a space that is already here, and in it you are neither Owner nor Administrator. Bringing a whole space back is a decision of whoever runs it, so ask them.
data.moreTitle: Take the data to another program
data.exportRecordsBody: One line per record, to open in Excel, Numbers or whatever you use.
data.manualBody: One file with everything, that you download and keep wherever you like.
data.alsoTheBackupHint: The backup becomes this file. Whatever is there and not here goes.
data.notAlsoTheBackupHint: Without it, only this browser changes. Next time, the backup will see the two sides differ and ask which one to keep.

destination.webdavHint: Nextcloud, ownCloud, Synology and most hosting panels speak WebDAV. It keeps a version of every file, so two devices saving at once do not run each other over.
destination.needsPermission: A browser only talks to this place if the server there allows it. A permission error means exactly that: allow the address of {{app}} there, or use Manual copy, Download a copy, up there, which needs nobody's permission.
destination.secretStaysHere: Kept in this browser only. None of it passes through any server of this project.
destination.unreachable: I could not reach the destination {{where}}. Check that you are online and that the address is right.
destination.refused: Access refused by the destination {{where}}. The token may have expired: sign in to the service again.
destination.answered: The destination {{where}} answered {{status}} and did not finish. Try again in a few minutes.
destination.databaseHint: The change log becomes rows in a table rather than a file. Two devices can write at the same time without one going over the other. Works with Turso or with a sqld you run yourself.
destination.databaseAddressHint: The address the service gave you, ending in turso.io, or the one of your own sqld. You can paste it the way Turso shows it, starting with libsql://, or just the host on its own.
destination.addressNotAnAddress: This address was not understood. Check that it starts with https:// and that nothing is missing from it.

importing.title: Import a statement
importing.explain: Pick the file, check what {{app}} understood, and only then write it down. Nothing is written before that.
importing.cannotWriteBody: Importing a statement is writing records, and your role in this space writes none. Ask whoever runs the space to change your role, if you need to import here.
importing.pickHint: A PDF invoice or receipt, CSV, OFX, QIF, XLSX or JSON. A {{app}} backup does not come in here: it goes back through Data, Restore from a file. The file does not leave this device.

kind.invoice: This looks like a card invoice
kind.unknown: I did not recognise what this document is

importing.saysTotal: and says it adds up to
importing.unsureTitle_one: 1 line I am not sure I understood
importing.unsureTitle_other: {{count}} lines I am not sure I understood
importing.unsureBody: A PDF does not arrive in columns, so some lines were read by deduction. They are marked, with the original text of the document beside them, so you can compare before writing anything.
importing.noText: This PDF holds no text, only a picture. That is usually a scan or a photograph. Ask the bank for the original file, or use the CSV, the OFX or the spreadsheet.
importing.accountHint: The whole file goes into this account.

chose.digits: I picked this one from the digits in the file. Change it if it is wrong.
chose.institution: I picked this one from the name of the bank in the document. Change it if it is wrong.
chose.onlyCard: It is an invoice, and this is your only card. Change it if it is wrong.
chose.onlyAccount: It is a statement, and this is your only account. Change it if it is wrong.
chose.remembered: It is the account the last file of this shape went into.
chose.cardDigits: Recognised by the four digits of the card.

importing.willSort: {{count}} arrive already sorted by your rules.
importing.allClear_one: Everything is ready: 1 record for {{account}}, nothing in doubt and nothing repeated. Just write it.
importing.allClear_other: Everything is ready: {{count}} records for {{account}}, nothing in doubt and nothing repeated. Just write it.
importing.columnsHint: If a column was read as the wrong thing, correct it here and the list below follows.
importing.duplicatesTitle_one: 1 looks like it is already here
importing.duplicatesTitle_other: {{count}} look like they are already here
importing.duplicatesBody: When the bank gave the same identifier the record comes unticked and locked. When only the day, the amount and the start of the description match, it is yours to decide.
importing.caption: Records read from the file, with date, description, amount and whether they are already here
importing.emptyTitle: I found no records in this file
importing.emptyBody: Check that this is the right statement, or correct the columns above.
importing.unreadable: I could not read this file. It may have arrived incomplete, or it may not be a statement.
importing.skippedTitle_one: See the line that was left out
importing.skippedTitle_other: See the {{count}} lines that were left out

reason.notUnderstood: holds money and names no day

importing.doneBody_one: It is in the space that is open, already sorted by your category rules.
importing.doneBody_other: They are in the space that is open, already sorted by your category rules.
importing.noAccountBody: A statement needs an account to go into. Create one under Accounts and come back.
importing.signAsWritten: Carry the sign the bank wrote
importing.signGuessedExpense: Nothing in this file is negative, so it looks like a card invoice, where every line is a purchase. If it is a statement, change it here.
importing.signHint: The file has amounts on both sides, so its sign is what counts.

finding.spentMoreThanEarned: This month {{over}} more went out than came in. You earned {{income}} and spent {{expense}}.
finding.categoryAboveUsual: {{subject}} is {{difference}} above its usual month. Usually {{usual}}, this month {{thisMonth}}.
finding.categoryBelowUsual: {{subject}} came in {{difference}} under its usual month: {{thisMonth}} against the usual {{usual}}.
finding.budgetPassed: The limit on {{subject}} is past by {{over}}. It was {{limit}} and {{spent}} has gone.
finding.budgetPace: At this rate {{subject}} ends the month at {{atThisRate}}, {{over}} over the limit. There is {{left}} left.
finding.subscriptionLoad_one: One charge repeats every month and takes {{everyMonth}}, or {{everyYear}} a year.
finding.subscriptionLoad_other: {{count}} charges repeat every month and add up to {{everyMonth}}, or {{everyYear}} a year. Worth opening the list and seeing which ones you use.
finding.subscriptionRose: {{subject}} went from {{was}} to {{now}}. That is {{everyYear}} more a year.
finding.chargedTwice_one: {{subject}} shows up twice at {{amount}}, one day apart. Check that it was not charged twice.
finding.chargedTwice_other: {{subject}} shows up twice at {{amount}}, {{count}} days apart. Check that it was not charged twice.
finding.thinReserve: You have {{onHand}} and spend {{usualExpense}} a month: that covers {{covers}} months. Three months is {{missing}} away, or {{everyMonth}} a month for a year.
finding.lowSavingRate: {{left}} is left of the {{income}} that comes in, {{percent}} per cent. Ten per cent would be {{wanted}}, which is {{missing}} away.
finding.invoiceOverBalance_one: The {{subject}} card invoice is {{amount}} and you have {{onHand}}. That is {{short}} short, and it is due tomorrow.
finding.invoiceOverBalance_other: The {{subject}} card invoice is {{amount}} and you have {{onHand}}. That is {{short}} short, and it is due in {{count}} days.
finding.duesOverBalance_one: One bill falls due in the next fortnight, of {{total}}. You have {{onHand}}, which is {{short}} short.
finding.duesOverBalance_other: {{count}} bills fall due in the next fortnight and add up to {{total}}. You have {{onHand}}, which is {{short}} short.
finding.goalStalled_one: {{subject}} has had nothing put into it for a day. {{still}} to go, or {{everyMonth}} a month to arrive on time.
finding.goalStalled_other: {{subject}} has had nothing put into it for {{count}} days. {{still}} to go, or {{everyMonth}} a month to arrive on time.
finding.idleCash: You have {{spare}} beyond three months of cover. Worth keeping that apart from the money you spend.
finding.idleCashLosing: You have {{spare}} beyond three months of cover. Standing still, it loses {{losing}} of buying power in a year, at the {{inflation}}% inflation of the last twelve published months.
finding.betterThanUsual: This month you spent {{saved}} less than usual: {{expense}} against the usual {{usual}}.

signTarget.savingRate: Reference: 10 per cent left over or more
signTarget.committed: Reference: up to half of what you have
signTarget.repeatingLoad: Reference: up to half of what comes in

said.coverDues: {{amount}} short of what falls due in the next days. That is this week, not the plan.
said.buffer_one: {{amount}} to go. At {{everyMonth}} a month, it takes one month.
said.buffer_other: {{amount}} to go. At {{everyMonth}} a month, it takes {{count}} months.
said.reserve_one: {{amount}} to go. At {{everyMonth}} a month, one month more.
said.reserve_other: {{amount}} to go. At {{everyMonth}} a month, {{count}} months more.
said.goal_one: {{amount}} to go. At {{everyMonth}} a month, it takes one month.
said.goal_other: {{amount}} to go. At {{everyMonth}} a month, it takes {{count}} months.
said.freeUpMonthly: {{amount}} more has to be left over each month. Until it is, nothing below moves.
said.undated: {{amount}} to go. With nothing left over in the month, this carries no date.

detail.tight: At least one of the four signs is poor. Start with the first one on the list, which is the one with the most money at stake.
detail.steady: Nothing is poor and something could still be better.
detail.tooSoon: Not enough records yet. Three full months is what it takes to read all four signs, and until then only what is due right now has an answer.

advisor.loggerBody: This reads the money of the whole household, and a Logger only ever sees the records they wrote. A verdict made of one part is not a smaller verdict: the measures were written for a household, so it would tell you your reserve covers nothing and ask you to put aside a month of the household spending. Your own records are under List, and your limits under Budget.
advisor.needMonths: This sign needs three full months, with what comes in and what goes out written down.
advisor.signsBody: Each one is a division between two figures you have seen on another screen. The reference sits under every reading.

said.savingRate: {{income}} comes in each month and {{expense}} goes out. That leaves {{left}}.
said.reserve: You have {{onHand}} and spend {{usualExpense}} a month. Three months would be {{wanted}}.
said.committed_one: One bill falls due in the next {{days}} days, of {{due}}, against the {{onHand}} you have.
said.committed_other: {{count}} bills fall due in the next {{days}} days and add up to {{due}}, against the {{onHand}} you have.
said.committedNone: Nothing falls due in the next {{days}} days.
said.repeatingLoad_one: One charge repeats every month and takes {{everyMonth}} of the {{income}} that comes in.
said.repeatingLoad_other: {{count}} charges repeat every month and add up to {{everyMonth}} of the {{income}} that comes in.
said.repeatingLoadNone: Nothing in your records repeats every month.

advisor.planBody: In order, with what it costs a month and when it finishes. All of it comes out of the same thing an ordinary month leaves over: {{surplus}}.
advisor.planStuckBody: In order, and what each one costs.
advisor.stuckBody: An ordinary month leaves nothing over, so nothing here carries a date: on what comes in today, none of these steps moves. The first thing is to make the month close.
advisor.late: That is past the date you set for this goal.
advisor.planDone: In this order, all of it is done by {{month}}.
advisor.trendBody: The {{count}} most recent closed months against the {{count}} before them.
advisor.trendCover: Since {{month}}, what you have went from {{before}} to {{now}} of ordinary spending.
advisor.cardUsual: An ordinary invoice is {{usual}}, {{share}}% of what comes in.

cardDirection.rising: The last one closed at {{latest}}, above the ordinary one.
cardDirection.falling: The last one closed at {{latest}}, below the ordinary one.
cardDirection.steady: The last one closed at {{latest}}, in line with the others.

advisor.aheadTotal: You already have {{total}} committed in instalments, out to {{month}}.
advisor.overSurplus: more than a month leaves over
advisor.aheadTight_one: One of those months is already spent past what an ordinary month leaves over, before it has begun.
advisor.aheadTight_other: {{count}} of those months are already spent past what an ordinary month leaves over, before they have begun.
advisor.exposureBody_one: The one source of income in your records, in an ordinary month.
advisor.exposureBody_other: The {{count}} sources of income in your records, in an ordinary month.
advisor.wouldLast: If {{name}} stopped, what you have today covers {{cover}} of ordinary spending.
advisor.wouldCover: If {{name}} stopped, what still comes in would cover an ordinary month.
advisor.seasonBody: The months of the year behind that cost more than an ordinary month of {{usual}}, and when they come round again.
advisor.seasonWas: That is what it cost in {{was}}, {{over}} above an ordinary month.
advisor.seasonSave_one: Putting {{everyMonth}} aside this month gets you there without a fright.
advisor.seasonSave_other: Putting {{everyMonth}} aside each of the next {{count}} months gets you there without a fright.
advisor.leversBody_one: The category that weighs most in an ordinary month, and the cheapest month you have had in it.
advisor.leversBody_other: The {{count}} categories that weigh most in an ordinary month, and the cheapest month you have had in each.
advisor.cheapestMonth: Your cheapest month was {{best}}, which is {{frees}} less.
advisor.sameEveryMonth: The same every month, with nothing to squeeze.
advisor.leversTotal: Repeating your own cheapest months would leave {{frees}} more over every month.
advisor.allTitle: What else the figures pointed at
advisor.allBody: In the order of what has the most money at stake.
advisor.nothingBody: There is nothing out of place in your records. That is good news, not a fault.
advisor.nothingYetBody: There are not enough months to compare against. As you write things down, the findings turn up here on their own.
advisor.how_one: All of this is arithmetic over your own records, one month of them, done on this device. There is no model, no score and no opinion about what you ought to want: every line carries the figures it was made from, so you can check it by hand.
advisor.how_other: All of this is arithmetic over your own records, {{count}} months of them, done on this device. There is no model, no score and no opinion about what you ought to want: every line carries the figures it was made from, so you can check it by hand.
advisor.assumes: The one opinion is the order of the plan: cover before a goal, because a household with no cover pays for the next bad week with a card. Beyond that, the arithmetic assumes the months ahead look like the months behind, and the dates redraw themselves as you write things down.
advisor.notAdvice: This is not investment advice. {{app}} reads what you wrote down and says what it found. Telling somebody where to put their money is a different job, done by people who are licensed to do it.

cards.title: Cards
cards.explain: The card is the plastic. The account is the money. A multiple card uses both: on credit it lands on the invoice, on debit it leaves the balance the same day.
cards.name: Name
cards.lastFourHint: It is how a statement names the card, and how an import recognises it. You can leave it empty.
cards.creditAccountHint: The credit card account the purchases land on.
cards.debitAccountHint: The account the money leaves the same day.
cards.needsDebitAccount: To add a debit or a benefit card, first create the account the money leaves.
cards.editDescription: The name, the digits and the accounts can be corrected. The kind does not change: a card of another kind is another card.
cards.fromAccounts: Cards are added in {{where}}, up there: choose the kind Card and say whether it is credit, debit or multiple. A second card on the same invoice comes in from the menu of the credit card, in {{add}}.
cards.noneAndNotYours: No cards yet. Adding one belongs to whoever runs the space.
cards.managedFromAccounts: To change or remove a card, use the menu of its account up there.
cards.removeKeeps: The records stay. Only the name of the card leaves them.
cards.addToThisInvoice: Add a card to this invoice
cards.addToInvoice: Add a card to the {{name}} invoice
cards.addToInvoiceDescription: Another card that charges the same invoice, like the extra card somebody else in the house carries. Its purchases go on the holder's invoice.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.explain: This is where the data actually leaves, and it cannot be undone. Nothing happens until you type the name. If you want to keep a copy, save one up there first.
danger.personalKeeps: Erases everything inside. The personal space stays, empty.
danger.sharedGoes: Erases everything inside, and the space stops existing here.
danger.notYoursToErase: Erasing {{name}} belongs to whoever owns it. You can leave the space, under Manage spaces.
danger.everythingHereBody: Erases the whole database of this browser: every space and the preferences. {{app}} comes back as if it were the first time.
danger.everythingServerBody: Erases every space that is yours. A space of somebody else you only leave, because their records are not yours to erase.
danger.confirmPersonalBody: The records, accounts, cards, categories, budgets, goals, rules, investments and the history of this space all go. The space itself stays, empty.
danger.confirmSharedBody: The records, accounts, cards, categories, budgets, goals, rules, investments and the history all go, and the space leaves your list. Whoever was in it on another device still has the copy they already have.
danger.confirmEverythingHereBody: The database file is erased from this browser. There is no copy anywhere else, other than the one you exported yourself and, if it is on, the automatic backup.
danger.confirmEverythingServerBody: Every space that is yours goes from the server. You leave the spaces of other people without erasing anything of theirs. Your account stays.
danger.spaceEmptied_one: {{name}} is empty now. 1 record was erased.
danger.spaceEmptied_other: {{name}} is empty now. {{count}} records were erased.
danger.alsoTheCopy: Also erase the copy kept at the destination ({{where}})
danger.alsoTheCopyHint: The copy of this space goes from the destination with it. The automatic backup stays on for the other spaces.
danger.keepTheCopyHint: The copy stays where it is, and the automatic backup is switched off because of it: with it on, the next run would see the destination as ahead and bring this whole space back.
danger.copyGone: The copy at the destination was erased too.
danger.copyWentFirst: The copy at the destination had already been erased, and the space is still here, whole. The backup is still on, so the next run writes the copy again.
danger.backupOff: The automatic backup was switched off, so the destination does not bring this space back.
danger.copyOutOfReachTitle: The copy at the destination is going to stay where it is
danger.copyOutOfReachBody: The address of the destination is not complete yet, so {{app}} cannot take the copy of this space away from it. Erasing here switches the automatic backup off: left on, this whole space would come back the moment somebody finished filling the address in.

auto.title: Automatic backup
auto.body: A copy of every space, kept up to date in a place of yours.
auto.onWithNowhereToWrite: The backup is on and the place is not filled in, so nothing is being copied. Fill the fields above, or switch it off.
auto.failed: I could not save the copy. Destination: {{where}}
auto.conflictWaiting: The backup of {{name}} is waiting for you to decide.
auto.conflictBody: Since they last agreed, this browser wrote {{here}} and the backup took in {{there}}. Nothing has been replaced.
auto.keepBothHint: The safe one, and the one that loses nothing: both sides end up with everything either of them wrote, record by record.
auto.undoSaved: The last two throw away what the other side wrote. Before either of them, a file with the side that is going is saved for you, and Restore from a file brings it back if you change your mind.

paper.title: {{space}}, {{month}}
paper.asItStood: The figures are as they stood on {{day}}, the last day of the month.
paper.yoursOnly: Your own records only. You are a Logger in this space, so these figures are what you yourself put through the accounts.
paper.chooseInReports: In the dialogue that opens, choose Save as PDF instead of a printer.
paper.moneyAtTheEnd: Money at the end of the month
paper.spendableAtTheEnd: Of that, there to be spent
paper.cardsCaption: The open invoice of each card
paper.savingCaption: The saving rule and the goals
paper.monthsAheadCaption: What the next months should add up to
paper.madeHere: Made on this device by {{app}}. Nothing left it to produce this file.

move.title: Move between accounts
move.explain: Money that leaves one of your accounts and goes into another. It is neither money out nor money in: the total of what you have does not change.
move.notHere: Credit cards and investment accounts are not here. A card's invoice is paid under Invoices, with Pay the invoice, which says which invoice was paid; an investment account is worth the holdings inside it.
move.repeats: Repeats every month, on this day

toMove.title: It was between your accounts
toMove.explain: Money that went from one of your accounts to another is neither money out nor money in. Say where the other end is and this becomes a move between accounts.
toMove.keeps: The day, the description and the bank's mark stay. The category, the card and the priority go, because moving money is not spending.
toMove.join: Join with "{{description}}", of {{day}}, which is the same money written on the other account. That record is deleted, so the money is not counted twice.
